successors.note: The Lordship page: Ibn Mardanish 'ceded the Taifa of Albarracín to a vassal of Sancho VI of Navarre' in 1167 and Pedro Ruiz de Azagra consolidated it in 1172; it passes via the Almoravids and Ibn Mardanish, not directly in 1104.

rulers.name: Yahya Husam ad-Dawla
rulers.note: List: 1103-1104; conquered by the Almoravids in 1104.

keyframe_review.note: 8,724 km2: the district of Albarracín; the page states no area ('Area: Not stated') and no territory, so the shape stands. Drawn from 1012, when the page starts the polity and its first ruler ('The polity existed from 1012 to 1104'); Cliopatria begins in 1015.
8,845 km2: one grid cell more on the east edge; the page dates no territorial change (Abu Marwan 'Abd al-Malik reigned 1045-1103).
8,773 km2: one cell fewer; the page is silent on 1066.
8,821 km2: the page is silent on 1085 (the year Alfonso VI took Toledo, a neighbour in Cliopatria's list); the Taifa overview ends it in 1104.

8,821 km2 for 1099-1110, but the page has 'The polity existed from 1012 to 1104' and 'conquest by the Almoravid dynasty in 1104' (the Taifa overview agrees: 'Albarracín: 1011-1104 (to Almoravids)'). Drawn to 1104; the land is Almoravid land afterwards. Yahya Husam al-Dawla ruled 1103-1104.

ledger.note: 1012: Albarracín becomes an independent taifa of the Banu Razin. 'The polity existed from 1012 to 1104, and was centered at the city of Albarracín'; key date 'Downfall of the Caliphate of Córdoba in 1012'; first ruler Hudayl 1012-1045 (the Taifa overview has 1011). The page names the city only.

1104: the Almoravids conquer Albarracín. Key date 'conquest by the Almoravid dynasty in 1104'; 'The polity existed from 1012 to 1104'; the Taifa overview: 'Albarracín: 1011-1104 (to Almoravids)'. Cliopatria keeps the taifa to 1110.

wars.name: Almoravid conquest of Albarracín
wars.outcome: Yahya Husam al-Dawla (1103-1104) was the last ruler; the Almoravids conquered the taifa in 1104.
wars.note: No campaign is described on the page; the Lordship page has the territory ceded by Ibn Mardanish to a vassal of Navarre in 1167.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a boundary for the taifa; the Sierra de Albarracín district is approximate throughout.

notes:
IDENTITY. 1012 to 1104 on the page ('The polity existed from 1012 to 1104'), the Taifa overview 1011-1104; Cliopatria 1015-1110. The infobox header says 'c. 1037' for the taifa kingdom's date, which the page's text contradicts. The page states no area and no territory ('Area: Not stated'), and names none of the neighbours, so the five Cliopatria shapes (all about 8,800 km2) rest on Cliopatria alone; differences between them are one or two grid cells and no event explains them.
UNSETTLED. (1) Page silent on the taifa's relations with Zaragoza, Toledo and Valencia (the Cliopatria neighbours) and on any parias to Castile or Aragon; none are written. (2) The 1104 conquest has no campaign on any page opened; the Almoravid dossier (another part) keeps Albarracín to 1110 in its own count and may need the 1104 year. (3) The Lordship of Albarracín (Sinyoría d'Albarrazín: Pedro Ruiz de Azagra 1167, independent 1172, Borja accords 1190, Aragonese conquest 1284, incorporated 1300) already has a dossier (lordship-of-albarracin, eu-12), which names the Murcia taifa as its predecessor. (4) The Murcia dossier records Albarracín under Ibn Mardanish until 1165-1168 (Spanish article), the Lordship page says the cession was in 1167.
PAGES. Taifa of Albarracín, Lordship of Albarracín, Taifa (overview): three pages; 'Banu Razin' does not exist as an English title (url_not_found).
GAZETTEER. 'Albarracín' is not in places.jsonl; the dossier uses Cliopatria's shape for every region.
